title: Random forests map landslide susceptibility in Ruijin, Jiangxi, China
summary: Random forest and support vector machine models were trained on 19 geo-environmental factors and 155 observed landslides, with three ways of processing categorical factors. The three random forest models reached overall accuracy of 89.61%, 91.47% and 94.54% on validation sets, clearly above the SVM models (81.79% to 83%). In a check against 26 landslides from 2017 to 2020, the weight-assignment random forest map placed 23 in high or very high susceptibility zones. One region, retrospective validation only.
ai_technology: Random forest and support vector machine models on 19 geo-environmental raster layers

evidence.tested: Hold-out validation sets (30%) and a check against 26 newer landslide events.
evidence.unknown: Transfer to other regions and operational use; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Predicts landslide occurrence probability for susceptibility zonation.
